removed_or_hidden: No fabricated testimonials, partner-logo wall, customer results, earned-income promises or real-example section.
No generated application screens, simulated social UI, fake installed vehicle advertising or decorative model.
No subscription price is invented for the public pitch; exact configured pricing remains in the plan destination.
No automatic-publishing claim, instant-payout language or claim that campaign spending is included in subscription fees.
Authentication and audience onboarding are destination previews with preserved intent, not a second account model.
No looping hero film control is shown when actual footage is unavailable.
implementation_steps: Build the public header, headline, audience actions and static photography first. These must render without enhancement or capture-generation services.
Generate the three authenticated browser captures from their actual Lab routes. Insert them into deterministic device/browser frames with explicit dimensions and readable Demo labels.
Create Recreate, Post and Drive as ordinary sections with complete HTML copy. Add one sticky desktop stage only at 1200px and above and only when its height fits the viewport.

Use IntersectionObserver to select the active explanatory source. Apply one requestAnimationFrame-throttled CSS scroll variable if geometric movement is enabled; never set React state every animation frame.
Build the business section from the two actual desktop captures and their readable external descriptions, not a fabricated product montage.
Reuse the actual Lab EarningsSummary read-only in Get paid, with conspicuous demo-money provenance and no paid payout. It is an explanation, not a public proof point.

Map Start earning to the /earn destination preview, For businesses to /for-business, and shared Get started to signup intent selection. Do not link the public business CTA directly to authenticated /business.
Record a short genuine product walkthrough only after the HTML interactions work. An external Play demo can open that recording if generated; otherwise Open example remains the working control.
Capture desktop and phone first folds, each earning chapter, the business comparison and Get paid. Record a short desktop scroll pass and repeat it with reduced motion.

story-loopday-01: same unmodified finished 9:16 master, 240×427px desktop and 180×320px phone.
vehicle-maya-01: 3:2 source, contained at 600×400px in the desktop Drive reservation and 358×239px on phone; label Demo vehicle · No installed ad.
Deterministic rear-door placement diagram: 160px reference width, 2px strokes, ordinary named-zone explanation; never projected onto the vehicle.
capture-business-home-1440 and capture-business-content-1440: actual browser-produced 1440×1000 captures, each in a 648px-wide desktop or 358px-wide phone browser frame.
The business captures visibly reuse the portrait, portfolio, car and delivered-file assets listed for their source screens. They do not create additional source-media records.
EarningsSummary is live read-only HTML using the existing Lab money fixture, not a generated screenshot or animated financial illustration.
motion_and_interaction: Hero text and audience actions are visible immediately. The default photograph never pretends to play. Public Open example controls respond with the shared 140ms control feedback.

At desktop chapter boundaries, source selection uses a 220ms crossfade. Optional scroll movement translates the explanatory assembly by at most 24px and rotates a device by at most 8 degrees around Y; it returns to 0 degrees before a recorded demo plays.
Sticky positioning is native CSS; scrolling is never prevented, accelerated, snapped between chapters or tied to a synthetic work-state timeline.
On phone, all chapter scenes remain in normal document flow with no scroll choreography. They need no reveal animation to become visible.
Menu opens the shared 320ms sheet, with visible Close, Escape support and focus return.

If actual public footage is supplied later, play one muted 12-second film only when visible and preferences permit: four 3-second shots of filming, supplied creative, real vehicle context and implemented content review. Provide immediate Pause and Replay; no autoplay audio. Otherwise retain the still and omit Play film.
Get paid never animates an amount, approval or payout status. Any recorded product walkthrough is explicitly started and labeled Demo.
Reduced motion removes autoplay, sticky choreography, translation and rotation, replacing the desktop sequence with three complete static chapter compositions in ordinary flow.

Desktop active Recreate, Post and Drive chapters under native scrolling.
Open and closed public navigation menu.

spec.money: The hero phone contains the same visibly labeled demo opportunity amounts as User Home, not a new earnings claim. Public HTML explains payment basis and approval conditions rather than advertising an income total. Get paid may show the actual implemented Lab summary with $78.40 available and a $50.00 requested payout, accompanied by Demo money · Not a customer result. There is no paid payout or count-up animation. Essential/Growth output counts are factual product inclusions; prices are omitted because no real settings value is supplied, and campaign spending is explicitly separate.
mock_data: All product captures use the same fictional Maya Chen and Loopday Coffee fixtures as the authenticated prototypes; no separate marketing-only customer records.
Public acquisition copy: Recreate. / Post. Drive. / Get paid.; Start earning; For businesses; Check the task, eligibility and approval conditions.
Recreate explanation: Film your version of a business's Reel. Post explanation: Share the supplied Story. Drive explanation: Carry an ad on your car. Monthly pay follows approved proofs.
Plan output copy: Essential 1 monthly shoot, 10 photos, 3 videos; Growth 2 monthly shoots, 20 photos, 6 videos. Campaign spending is separate from your content subscription.
Demo EarningsSummary reads the same available 7840-cent and requested-payout 5000-cent fields as Profile; it never creates a new balance for the public site.
No customer testimonials, production logos, real installed-ad records or consented case studies are available; omit that section entirely.
Public route intents are earn and business preselection within the shared onboarding model, not separate account types.
spec.depth_and_technology: The public site uses one physical phone frame meeting a filming scene, then one explanatory source stage whose material changes with the task. Depth is limited to the useful overlap, the supplied creative and browser frames. Solid CSS planes provide the stage; no atmospheric generated background or glow. A genuine identity-matched vehicle model may replace the Drive photo only after explicit activation and only with permissioned model data, using the Profile viewer lighting and camera rules in a maximum 640×400px stage. The baseline needs no model, footage or WebGL. Keep at most one active canvas/player, dynamically load optional three.js only on request, cap DPR at 1.5 and render on demand.
